section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that at the Giving of the Torah, a new level of self-nullification called "to say" was granted, surpassing the prior self-nullification of "we will do and we will hear."
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "And G-d spoke all these words, saying,"
And it is explained in Chassidus,
that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given that a person's study of Torah should be in the manner of "to say,"
to repeat the matters that the Holy One, blessed be He, says.
"My tongue shall answer Your word."
For seemingly,
behold, even before the Giving of the Torah, Israel preceded "we will do" to "we will hear,"
for the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" is the self-nullification of the one who possesses will,
and what is the innovation in the self-nullification of "to say" that was renewed at the Giving of the Torah, relative to the self-nullification of "we will do and we will hear"?
And the explanation of this is,
that the self-nullification of the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" has an advantage.
For the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear" is the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom,
and through the people accepting the yoke of His kingdom, He becomes King.
[And this is analogous to the self-nullification of the chariot,
that through the self-nullification of the chariot to the rider, thereby
it carries and elevates the rider.]
But the self-nullification of "to say" that was renewed at the Giving of the Torah is self-nullification to the ultimate degree.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given for the fulfillment of commandments to be in ultimate self-nullification, where the command itself compels the person to be as commanded.
section.t: And likewise is it regarding the fulfillment of the commandments,
that at the Giving of the Torah, the power was given that a person's fulfillment of the commandments should be in ultimate self-nullification,
meaning that his fulfillment of the commandments should be
(not because he accepted upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of heaven and the yoke of the commandments,
but rather)
because the command of the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees upon him to be according to the command.
And as explained in Likkutei Torah
regarding the Ten Commandments that were said at the Giving of the Torah
[and likewise is it regarding all the commands in the Torah]
that they were said in the language of a command and also in the future tense,
for the speech itself decrees upon the person and the world
(and compels them)
to be so.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two advantages of the self-nullification in fulfilling commandments through the command's compulsion over the self-nullification of accepting the yoke.
section.t: And it may be said that the advantage of the self-nullification of fulfilling commandments in this manner, relative to the self-nullification of accepting the yoke,
is in two matters.
Because the self-nullification of accepting the yoke is through his having accepted upon himself to be a servant of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
And beyond this,
that the self-nullification of a servant to his master
[even when he is born a servant]
is connected to his own existence,
for his essence is that he is a servant of the master,
but the self-nullification in the aforementioned manner is
(not from the aspect of the person's essence,
but rather)
that it is impossible for there to be an existence in the world that is contrary to the command of the Holy One, blessed be He.
